AGENT-GENERATED FEEDBACK from a Grok 4.6 session on one of Alex's projects (2026-08-13, two entries: a remaining-MVP readout and an encouragement capture session), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14. Produced by telling the agent *"reflow2 is still a development project - please note any issues or gaps or opportunities to improve reflow2 at path/to/feedback.md"*.

⭐⭐⭐ THE REASON THIS NODE EXISTS: **FOUR OF ITS ITEMS WERE INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED BY A DIFFERENT AGENT (Claude Opus 5), ON A DIFFERENT GRAPH (reflow2's own), IN A SESSION THAT HAD NOT READ THE FEEDBACK.** One agent reporting friction is an opinion; two agents on different models and different designs hitting the same edges is a defect report.

═══ ✅ CORROBORATED — hit in this session before the file was read ═══

**1. THE NEAR-DUPLICATE GUARD FIRES ON SIBLINGS AND ACROSS NODE TYPES** (their items 1 and 2, second entry). Six refusals in one capture session, every one of them a genuine non-duplicate:
  · a Requirement refused because its OWN governing Decision was "close"
  · a Capability refused because the Requirement it satisfies was "close"
  · a Requirement refused because a Capability created MINUTES EARLIER in the same batch was "close"
  · one Decision refused TWICE, each refusal naming a DIFFERENT batch of near-matches — the declared ones are excluded and the next-nearest surface, so `distinct_from` grows by retry
⇒ **A Requirement, the Decision that governs it and the Capability that satisfies it are the GOLDEN THREAD. They are supposed to share wording.** A guard that reads them as candidate duplicates fires hardest on exactly the capture pattern the skills prescribe. Their words: *"Each refusal named a sibling I had just created, not a true duplicate."*

**2. `add_decision` CANNOT MERGE WITHOUT RESENDING THE BODY** (their item 3, second entry). Schema requires `id` + `name` + `decision`. Confirmed by cost, not just by reading: prepending a DECIDED header to three already-written decisions this session meant resending ~7 KB bodies verbatim each time. Their report adds the sharper risk: **the loop hint on such a merge still reads *"a Decision lands `proposed`"* even when merging an ACCEPTED node** — observed here too, status correctly stayed `accepted`, but the hint invites an agent to "fix" a status that was never wrong.

**3. CAPTURING CORRECTLY INFLATES THE LOOP DEBT** (their item 5, second entry). Their measurement: 62 → 66 never-asked gaps after a capture session, because each new `planned` Capability immediately owes a verification it cannot yet have. **Measured identically here: 74 → 79 gaps across this session's captures.** Their sentence is exact: *"this session created more of them by doing capture correctly."*

**4. `get_node` MISSES SILENTLY** (their item 5, first entry). REPRODUCED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH: `get_node {node_type: Project, id: "proj:does-not-exist-12345"}` returns `{"node": null}` with no hint — **and this graph holds exactly ONE Project, `proj:reflow2`.** That is precisely the case they describe: *"A miss on a type that has total: 1 should name the existing id."* ⚠️ A NEARBY EDGE, hit here the same day: passing `node_id` instead of `id` is REFUSED loudly and helpfully (*"unknown field `node_id`, expected `node_type` or `id`"*). So a malformed ARGUMENT is diagnosed and a missing NODE is not — the wrong way round, since the second is the commoner mistake.

═══ ⚠️ NOT REPRODUCED HERE — recorded so it is not treated as confirmed ═══

**`get_instructions` TRUNCATION** (their item 6, first entry): they report ~22.6 KB cut mid-sentence, with the standing rules after the cut never arriving — serious, because the repo file is only a pointer. **Called here the same day and the payload arrived COMPLETE**, ending cleanly on its closing line. ⇒ Likely CLIENT-SPECIFIC (an MCP payload budget in their harness) rather than server-side, which makes it a worse defect in one way: it is invisible from this side and the affected agent cannot tell that rules are missing. Their mitigation — serve it in named sections — survives regardless of cause.

═══ 📌 THEIR ITEMS NOT YET ASSESSED HERE ═══

First entry: (1) *"what is left to build?" is not a first-class query* — `what_next` ranks open DECISIONS, and a graph with one open Decision and a large build backlog gets nothing useful; four sources disagreed (Decision prose, Capability `status`, computed delivery, the repo). (2) status-vs-computed-delivery drift. (3) top gaps are hygiene, not product work — wrong default ranking for *"what do we build next?"*. (4) two sources of truth on one increment. (7) orientation tax. (8) *"the loop and the delivery plan share a dashboard and they should not."* (9) **decision-as-checklist is invisible to the temporal axis** — they propose a detector for an accepted Decision whose statement is a running delivery list with no `SCHEDULED_FOR` edges. Second entry: (4) `detect_gaps(scope)` explodes via Project CONTAINS at depth 3 and returns unrelated planned work rather than the seed's own thread.

📌 THEIR OWN PROCESS GAPS, WORTH KEEPING BECAUSE THEY ARE HONEST: they did not run `compare_designs` or `detect_gaps`, guessed a Project id rather than scanning, and did not export after graph writes — the last being the same omission `fact:second-user-first-run-report-2026-08-13` is about.

⚠️ THEIR KIT SIDECAR READ `0.11.0` / `0ec473e` (a 2026-07-25 tarball) WHILE THE LIVE SERVER SERVED A MUCH NEWER SURFACE. **Third independent signal that consumers run stale kits** — with `fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`, which concluded the same about Alex from different evidence. Their suggestion: write the running binary identity where `loop_status` or `graph_report` already expose it (`served_by` exists on `graph_report`).
